# PoC A — HTTP ingress into a durable Temporal-backed Node-RED flow

**Status: disposable prototype on branch `poc/http-ingress`. Not for merge as
production code.**

## Goal

Prove that an ordinary HTTP request can act as fire-and-forget ingress into a
durable Node-RED flow executed as a Temporal Workflow: the HTTP caller gets an
immediate 202 (with `workflowId`/`runId`), while the flow itself keeps running
durably — surviving both the ingress process and the Activity worker process
being killed.

## Files created (all under this directory; nothing else touched)

```
packages/node_modules/@tbrandenburg/node-red-temporal-runtime/poc/http-ingress/
├── async-server.js   # Express POST /poc/async -> starts executeFlow Workflow, returns 202
├── flow.json         # PoC flow: inject -> function -> delay(3s) -> change -> debug
└── README.md         # this file
```

`git diff --stat` (from repo root) at the end of this session:

```
$ git status --short
?? packages/node_modules/@tbrandenburg/node-red-temporal-runtime/poc/
```

No files under `packages/node_modules/@node-red/` were touched.

## Environment / ports used

| Component | Command / config |
|---|---|
| Temporal dev server | `temporal server start-dev --port 7239 --ui-port 8239 --db-filename /tmp/poc-http-ingress-a-temporal.db` |
| Combined worker (Node-RED + Activity + Workflow) | `TEMPORAL_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1:7239 TEMPORAL_WORKFLOW_TASK_QUEUE=poc-http-ingress-a TEMPORAL_ACTIVITY_TASK_QUEUE=poc-http-ingress-a node bin/node-red-temporal --flow poc/http-ingress/flow.json` |
| Ingress server | `TEMPORAL_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1:7239 TEMPORAL_WORKFLOW_TASK_QUEUE=poc-http-ingress-a TEMPORAL_ACTIVITY_TASK_QUEUE=poc-http-ingress-a POC_HTTP_PORT=3939 node poc/http-ingress/async-server.js` |

Task queue `poc-http-ingress-a` and Temporal port `7239`/UI `8239` were
dedicated to this PoC to avoid clashing with any parallel PoC B run on the
same machine. No Node-RED editor/admin API was ever started (the CLI's
default `bootstrap()` leaves `httpAdminRoot: false` unless `--admin-port` is
passed), so there was no editor port to worry about either.

All long-running processes were started with `setsid ... &` (not just
`nohup`) so they fully detach from the calling shell's session — plain
`nohup ... &` was NOT sufficient in this sandbox (the tool wrapper's shell
still waited on/killed the child on tool-call teardown); `setsid` fixed it.
PIDs were captured immediately after each `setsid` launch and used for every
subsequent kill (never pattern-killed).

## Flow used (`flow.json`)

```
n1 (inject, start) -> n2 (function: tag receivedAt) -> n5 (delay 3s)
   -> n3 (change: tag "poc-http-ingress-complete") -> n4 (debug, terminal)
```

Note: the delay was reduced from an initial 8s to 3s — see "Surprises" below
for why.

## Experiments

### A1 — basic request mapping — **PASS**

Command:
```
curl -s -w "\nHTTP_STATUS:%{http_code} TIME:%{time_total}s\n" \
  -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:3939/poc/async?foo=bar&baz=qux' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-Poc-Test: hello-world' \
  -d '{"user":"tom","action":"ping"}'
```
Result:
```
{"workflowId":"poc-http-ingress-1789914187802","runId":"01a0bf33-0821-7d1f-8b18-1b3dfa71ef35"}
HTTP_STATUS:202 TIME:0.035603s
```

Evidence — decoded Workflow input (`temporal workflow show --output json`,
first event's `input.payloads[0].data`, base64-decoded), showing the header,
query string, and JSON body all arrived intact inside `startMsg.payload`:
```json
{
  "startMsg": {
    "payload": {
      "method": "POST",
      "url": "/poc/async?foo=bar&baz=qux",
      "headers": {
        "host": "127.0.0.1:3939",
        "user-agent": "curl/8.5.0",
        "accept": "*/*",
        "content-type": "application/json",
        "x-poc-test": "hello-world",
        "content-length": "30"
      },
      "query": { "foo": "bar", "baz": "qux" },
      "body": { "user": "tom", "action": "ping" }
    }
  }
}
```
The Workflow itself also `COMPLETED` (`lastNode: "n4"`, the debug node),
confirming the envelope propagated through the whole flow.

### A2 — immediate acknowledgement — **PASS**

Same request as A1, timed: `TIME:0.035603s` (curl round-trip), against a 3s
`delay` node in the flow — the HTTP response returned ~85x faster than the
delay duration, without ever awaiting `handle.result()` in `async-server.js`.

### A3 — kill ingress after 202 — **PASS**

```
$ curl -s -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:3939/poc/async?exp=a3' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"exp":"A3"}'
{"workflowId":"poc-http-ingress-1789914242055","runId":"01a0bf33-dc0c-7ca8-abfb-e6dd4e740ace"}

$ kill 2131686   # async-server.js PID, killed immediately after the 202
$ ps -p 2131686
    PID TTY          TIME CMD          # (empty — process confirmed dead)

$ sleep 4  # past the 3s delay
$ temporal workflow describe --address 127.0.0.1:7239 \
    --workflow-id poc-http-ingress-1789914242055
Results:
  RunTime         3.49s
  Status          COMPLETED
  Result          {"flowVersion":"...","lastNode":"n4"}
```
The Workflow ran to completion entirely without the ingress process alive.

### A4 — restart Activity worker mid-flight — **PASS**

Started a fresh Workflow directly via `@temporalio/client` (bypassing the
ingress server, which was already dead from A3), then killed the combined
worker (PID `2132600`) ~4s after start — while the `delay` Activity (`n5`)
was already `Started` on that worker:

```
$ temporal workflow describe ... --workflow-id poc-http-ingress-a4-1789914271286
Pending Activities: 1
  ActivityId          node:n5:1
  Type                executeNode
  State               Started
  Attempt             1
  MaximumAttempts     3
  LastWorkerIdentity  2132600@tom-nuc7   # the worker PID just killed
```

Restarted a new combined worker process (PID `2133901`) on the same task
queue, then polled until completion:

```
$ temporal workflow describe ... --workflow-id poc-http-ingress-a4-1789914271286
RunTime         34.82s
Status          COMPLETED
```

The Workflow reached `COMPLETED` after the restarted worker picked up the
retried Activity. The ~30s gap between the kill and completion matches
`executeNode`'s configured `startToCloseTimeout: "30s"` in `lib/workflows.js`
— Temporal doesn't detect the dead worker via heartbeat (no heartbeat is
configured), it simply waits out the Activity's `startToCloseTimeout` before
retrying (`retry: { maximumAttempts: 3, initialInterval: "1s",
backoffCoefficient: 2 }`), then a freshly-polling worker claims the retry.

### A5 — Temporal history contains only serializable data — **PASS**

Same decoded payload as A1 (workflow start input) — the entire `startMsg`
is plain JSON (`method`/`url`/`headers`/`query`/`body` strings, objects, and
arrays only). No socket/req/res/stream reference, no function, no class
instance anywhere in the history. This is guaranteed structurally by
`async-server.js`'s `toEnvelope()`, which only ever reads `req.method`,
`req.originalUrl`, spreads `req.headers`/`req.query` into plain objects, and
takes the already-parsed (by `express.json()`) `req.body` — never passing
`req`/`res` themselves into the Workflow input.

## Surprises / deviations from the plan

1. **Default per-node Activity capture timeout (5000ms) is shorter than a
   "realistic" delay demo.** The flow originally used an 8s `delay` node (to
   mirror `demo/flows.recovery-demo.json`), which immediately failed with
   `[NODE_TIMEOUT] capture timed out after 5000ms` — `lib/capture.js`'s
   `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` (5000ms) is not currently exposed via the CLI or any
   env var, only via `captureOptions` passed to `createActivityWorker` in
   code. Reduced the delay to 3s to fit under this default rather than
   patching shared runtime code (out of scope / do-not-touch for this PoC).
   This is a real limitation worth flagging separately: any node whose
   per-invocation processing legitimately takes >5s (a real `delay` node
   included) will fail today unless a caller wires a custom
   `captureOptions.timeoutMs` through `createActivityWorker`/
   `createCombinedWorker`, which the stock CLI doesn't expose.
2. **`nohup ... &` alone was not enough to survive the bash tool's own
   timeout teardown** in this sandboxed environment — the first worker
   launch attempt was killed via SIGTERM when the *tool call* (not the
   background process itself) hit its 120s timeout. Switching to
   `setsid ... &` (per the `detach` skill) fixed this; PIDs were captured
   immediately after each `setsid` launch.
3. **The Node-RED `debug` node's console output was not visible in the
   worker's captured stdout log**, even with `console: true` on the node and
   the flow otherwise executing correctly end-to-end (confirmed via Temporal
   workflow history/result instead). Not investigated further — out of
   scope for this PoC, whose evidence came from Temporal's own history/
   `describe`/`show` output rather than Node-RED's console.
4. A parallel, unrelated PoC B process (`poc-http-ingress-b`) was observed
   running on the same machine during this session (different task queue,
   different flow path) — confirmed via `ps aux` that it was left untouched
   throughout.
